deities: Bharat Mata (Mother India; first-floor shrine with a large map of India)

history.dynasty: None (modern temple founded by Swami Satyamitranand Giri; run by the Samanvaya Sewa Trust)
history.summary: Bharat Mata Mandir is the famous eight-storey, 180-ft temple dedicated to Bharat Mata (Mother India) beside Samanvaya Kutir on the banks of the Ganga, founded by Swami Satyamitranand Giri (former Shankaracharya of Jyotirmath, Padma Bhushan 2015) and inaugurated by Prime Minister Indira Gandhi in 1983. It is a Hindu-organization temple, not a traditional shrine: each of its eight floors celebrates a theme of Indian nationhood and culture - Bharat Mata with a big map of India (1st floor); Shoor Mandir honouring freedom heroes like Gandhi, Subhash Chandra Bose, Shivaji, Rani Lakshmi Bai and Bhagat Singh (2nd); Matru Mandir honouring revered women (3rd); Sant Mandir honouring saints of different faiths including Buddha, Mahavira, Shankaracharya, Vivekananda, Guru Nanak and Kabir (4th); paintings of India's history and of all religions (5th); Shakti Mandir (6th); Vishnu avatars (7th); and a Shiva shrine (8th), whose terrace gives panoramic views of Haridwar. Its message is national unity beyond caste, creed and religion. Access to the upper floors is by lift (small fee, ascent only) with descent by stairs.

town_description: Haridwar, in the Haridwar district of Uttarakhand at the foothills of the Sivalik Hills where the Ganga enters the plains, is one of Hinduism's seven holy cities (Sapta Puri) and one of the four Kumbh Mela sites. Its spiritual heart is Har Ki Pauri, where the evening Ganga Aarti draws thousands daily. Mansa Devi and Chandi Devi temples crown the twin hills (Bilwa Parvat and Neel Parvat) overlooking the city, while the Maya Devi temple sits near Birla Ghat and Daksheshwar Mahadev lies in the adjoining heritage township of Kankhal.

travel.airport: Jolly Grant Airport, Dehradun (approx. 35-40 km; taxis available).
travel.railway: Haridwar Junction (approx. 2-4 km; autos and rickshaws available).
travel.road: On the banks of the Ganga near Samanvaya Kutir, reachable by auto-rickshaw and taxi from Har Ki Pauri and Kankhal; parking available on site. Lift ascent carries a small fee (approx. Rs. 2), descent by stairs.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; early mornings and evenings for a pleasant visit. Photography is allowed.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Opening hours conflict across sources (verify): 8:00 AM-8:00 PM (April-September) and 8:00 AM-7:00 PM (October-March) vs 6:00 AM-8:00 PM vs 7:00 AM-12:00 PM and 4:00-8:00 PM. No entry fee.
